subject: Subprocessor disclosure (limited) and onshore routing options
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finpartner.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor roster (limited) + onshore routing options

Hi Michael,

Thanks for taking this — FinPartner is doing a final privacy sign-off for our deployment and we need two things before Procurement can finish the PO: (1) a current subprocessor roster we can share with our internal privacy team (we're happy to treat it as confidential), and (2) a confirmation of whether traffic for our US and EU tenants can be pinned to onshore processing (or at least routed to US-only infrastructure) while we finalize residency controls.

We have a short security questionnaire but to be efficient we'd prefer a minimal disclosure file rather than the full vendor DPA annex (PII: list of vendor names, country of processing, and whether each vendor holds customer data or telemetry only). If you can indicate which processors support KMS/HSM-backed key separation, that would also help.

Can you share a version we can provide to legal by EOD Tue (US time)? If you need an NDA addendum or redaction guidance, tell me and we'll accomodate.

Appreciate it,
Samantha Lee
Head of Integrations, FinPartner
[signed]

[Attachment: FP_questionnaire_v1.docx]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finpartner.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster (limited) + onshore routing options

Samantha —

Thanks, and understood. I'm attaching a redacted subprocessor roster intended for customer consumption (see attached PDF). It lists processor name, country/region of primary processing, and a short note about data access scope ("customer data", "telemetry/ops"). For a few operational partners we classify as "sensitive" and have provided a high-level tag rather than a full location — happy to provide more under NDA.

Regarding onshore routing: we can pin routing by account at the edge and guarantee US-only processing for the request path and model execution for accounts on our Dedicated or Private plans. For Hosted customers we offer region pinning as a configuration and an additional contractual addendum that limits cross-border fallbacks.

I've asked Naomi to confirm KMS/HSM attestation status for the processors we list as handling customer data. Kimberly is looped to confirm whether we should propose a DPA amendment or a separate addendum for the residency commitment.

Next steps:
- Attached: subprocessor_roster_public_20261028.pdf (redacted for customer distribution)
- Naomi to confirm KMS/HSM support and provide evidence tags
- Kimberly to advise on proposed wording for an addendum or exhibit

Can you confirm if the redacted roster format is sufficient for FinPartner's legal? If not, let me know what additional fields you need and whether an NDA amendment would be accepted.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Account Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: subprocessor_roster_public_20261028.pdf]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster (limited) + onshore routing options

Michael / Kimberly —

Quick notes from security ops:
- I reviewed the redacted roster. For the entries tagged "customer data" we can provide a short attestation statement indicating which processors use KMS-managed keys vs. HSM-backed KMS. For a subset of partners (EdgeMetrics, TelemetryHub) we cannot provide HSM attestations because they use vendor-managed keys; we can, however, offer encrypted transit + limited access logs.
- Evidence: we can produce screenshots and an exported audit log extract (redacted) for two representative months. That usually satisfies procurement for onshore routing commitments.
- Onshore routing feasibility: for Dedicated and Private we can ensure model execution and data residency in the US region; for Hosted there is a fallback window in cross-region failover (contractually limitable).

I'll prepare a one-page attestation (KMS/HSM matrix) and a small packet with redacted audit exports if FinPartner needs it. Michael, do you want that packaged with the roster or provided as an "evidence on request" link?

Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: dataflow_onshore_map.png]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finpartner.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster (limited) + onshore routing options

Samantha / all —

Legal here. A few practical items:
1) The redacted roster Michael provided looks fine for an initial vendor review. If FinPartner requires more granularity (e.g., exact sub-processor street address or contractual flow-down copy) we will need either a mutual NDA extension or a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) exhibit that allows for limited disclosure under specific controls.
2) For onshore routing / residency commitments we can propose an Exhibit A (Residency & Routing) that commits Redwood to US-only model execution for the named FinPartner tenant and describes acceptable fallback conditions. That exhibit is typically coupled with an SLA and a small operational fee for dedicated capacity.
3) Export controls: if FinPartner has regulatory constraints (FIN regulations or export-limited data), we should capture that in the exhibit. Please confirm the level (PII, regulated financial identifiers, aggregated telemetry only).

If acceptable, I'll draft a short DPA amendment and route it for internal approval. Michael: happy to use Naomi's attestation as an annex to the amendment.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finpartner.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Final: limited roster + next steps for routing addendum

Samantha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Kimberly and Naomi's notes: attached is the customer-facing roster and a one-page KMS/HSM attestation (packaged as evidence on request). We can either:
A) Proceed with the redacted roster + evidence-on-request (no contract change).
B) Execute a short DPA Exhibit (Residency & Routing) that guarantees US-only execution for the FinPartner tenant with defined fallback windows; this path is what we recommend if you need contractual guarantees rather than operational assurances.

If you choose B, Kimberly will send a draft exhibit and we can route it through DocuSign. I've included a DocuSign link for an example addendum in the metadata.

Please let me know which option Procurement prefers and whether FinPartner will accept a redacted audit export as proof. If you want the extra evidence ahead of contracting, Naomi can upload the packet to a secure share; we'll only provide the full audit extracts after an NDA amendment.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call with legal/procurement early next week to close this.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Account Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: subprocessor_roster_public_20261028.pdf, dataflow_onshore_map.png]
